Top of the Morning
 

Illustration: Brendan Lynch/Axios
 

The AI safety debate is nuanced. Unfortunately, the politics of it are not.

The big picture: The partisan lines aren't perfectly drawn, but red tends to mean go and blue tends to mean stop.

  • Part of this is just a natural byproduct of each party's traditional stands on government regulation of big business.
  • Part is the personalities involved, particularly the Silicon Valley venture capitalists and tech execs who lined up hard behind Trump — either explicitly during the campaign or implicitly via subsequent donations to the inauguration or White House ballroom.
  • As with most things Trump, there is an equal and opposite reaction. In this case, it's Democrats seeking to slam the brakes on AI harder than Dario at his most doomy.

Zoom in: All of this could prove to be a massive self-own by the AI industry and its investors. Short-term expediency at the expense of long-term pragmatism.

  • There's been lots of talk about how AI is impacting the midterms — particularly as a reaction to data centers — but less on what happens afterwards.
  • This isn't an argument that the AI industry in 2024 should have anticipated a blue wave in 2026, or even that one is necessarily coming, but more a reminder of why prior generations of tech execs tried to stay on the political sidelines as much as possible.

Behind the scenes: If Democrats do win big in November, it's possible that both parties will get further entrenched on AI policy — battling over product liability and antitrust law.

  • It's also possible that some Republicans might view AI as an electoral problem, thus further eroding the industry's D.C. influence.
  • And it's not just about how politicians treat AI. It's also about how voters view it, largely lining up with their respective tribes.

The bottom line: The future of the world — quite literally — shouldn't be decided from partisan bunkers.
 
 
The BFD
 

Illustration: Shoshana Gordon/Axios
 

Joe Baratta is stepping down as Blackstone's global head of private equity strategies.

Why it's the BFD: Baratta is in charge of the private equity market's biggest book, helping to build it over three decades, and his departure seems to signal Blackstone's hierarchical shift away from star dealmakers.

Zoom in: Blackstone doesn't plan to fill Baratta's position. Instead, the private equity business will be run by the various unit heads who reported to him.

The bottom line: "Broader changes have been afoot at Blackstone, which [CEO Jon] Gray aims to transform into a money manager for the masses and a major player in the retirement market." — Bloomberg
 
 
Venture Capital Deals
 

• Instinct, a developer of general-purpose AI agents (i.e., rival to Meta's Muse), raised $1b at a $10b post-money valuation from Sequoia Capital, Benchmark Capital, and Coatue. axios.link/4z5a4Mf

• SiMa.ai, a San Jose, Calif.-based physical AI startup, raised $150m in Series C funding at a $1.45b post-money valuation. Fidelity and Amplify led, joined by Alter Venture Partners, Dell Technologies Capital, Maverick Capital, +ND Capital, Point72, StepStone Group, AllianceBernstein, Baron Capital, JPMorgan, and the State of Michigan. axios.link/3Vb5pK1

• Erad, a Saudi financing platform for SMEs, raised $22m in Series A funding. MEVP led, joined by SVC, 500 Global, S60 Ventures, ANB Capital, Conjunction Capital, Araya Ventures, Khwarizmi, Nuwa Capital, Aljazira Capital, Oraseya, and Joa Capital. axios.link/4rwDJet

• Complaion, an Italian provider of regulatory compliance solutions for SMEs, raised €13.5m. Eurazeo and Italian Founders Fund led, joined by Shapers, 2100 Ventures, Kfund, Sella Direct Ventures, Enzo Ventures, Vento, Ithaca, Eden Ventures, and Vesper. axios.link/4AtpxHg

• Feather, an East Palo Alto, Calif.-based hardware and developer platform for humanoid robots, raised $7.6m in pre-seed funding. Gradient led, joined by Builder Capital, Geometry, Seed Innovation, and Virgo VC. axios.link/4d6D9ya

Private Equity Deals
 

• Apax Partners is in talks to buy Warburg Pincus out of its stake in Dutch telco Odido, which would get around a €6.5b enterprise value, per the FT. axios.link/4z4AldC

• Coalesce Capital invested in ClearDefense, a provider of residential pest control services in the Southeast. axios.link/3TsGu44

• CVC Capital Partners said it won't make a new offer for British heat treatment firm Bodycote (LSE: BOY), clearing the path for Veritas Capital's £1.85b agreement. axios.link/4xHZ7Pn

• Greenbriar Equity Group is in talks to buy Spectrum Control, a Fairview, Pa.-based maker of radio frequency and microwave parts, from AEA Investors for more than $1.8b, per Bloomberg. axios.link/3VCUmcx

• GTCR acquired Tactacam, a Decorah, Iowa-based maker of cellular-connected cameras for the outdoor and security markets, from Bertram Capital for more than $1b. axios.link/47nluio

• PrimeSource Brands, backed by Clearlake Capital Group, acquired JACLO, a Cranford, N.J.-based distributor of plumbing products and decorative bath fixtures. axios.link/4rCoUr5

• Relation Insurance Services, backed by BayPine, acquired the assets of LaPlaca Insurance, a Chalfont, Pa.-based provider of business insurance, employee benefits, and personal lines. axios.link/4yhRdNH

• Siris agreed to merge industrial inkjet portfolio company EFI with the digital printing business of Agfa-Gevaert (Brussels: AGFB), with Siris to hold a 60% stake in the combined unit. Separately, Siris is investing for a 19.1% stake in Agfa-Gevaert. axios.link/4z1Y26a

• Warburg Pincus sweetened its takeover bid for Ingenia Communities (ASX: INA), an Australian operator of retirement communities and holiday parks, to US$1.5b. axios.link/4z0yg24
 
 
Public Offerings
 

Two large U.S. IPOs are expected this week: Oura and Accelevation.

• Bluerock Acquisition II, a Web3-focused SPAC, raised $150m in its IPO. axios.link/4dZwDJQ

⚡ Holtec, a Jupiter, Fla.-based nuclear power engineering company, withdrew its IPO registration — one week after postponing an offering that would have raised $825m at a $9.35b market cap at the midpoint. axios.link/3TXZO9v

• Solidigm, the NAND memory unit of SK Hynix, reportedly is prepping a 2027 IPO that could value the business at more than $100b. axios.link/4AspuLQ

• TCGX Acquisition II, an Asia health care SPAC, filed for a $100m IPO. axios.link/4AxjXUt

• Utmost Group, an Oaktree-backed provider of insurance-based wealth solutions, is delaying its London IPO plans, per Bloomberg. axios.link/46SEoNY
 
 
Liquidity Events
 

🚑 Audax Private Equity and Linden Capital Partners sold StatLab, a McKinney, Texas-based maker of consumables and reagents for anatomic pathology labs, to Danaher (NYSE: DHR) subsidiary Leica Biosystems. axios.link/4htnoTb

• Audax Private Equity agreed to sell GCG, a Chicago-based provider of specialty wire and cable, to Rexel (Paris: RXL). axios.link/4ABJqfh

• EQT reportedly hired JPMorgan to find a buyer for its control stake in Spanish theme park operator Parques Reunidos, valued at around €1.7b. axios.link/4hOK15T

• NetApp (Nasdaq: NTAP) agreed to acquire Peak A10, a U.K. metadata architecture and parallel file system provider, from Pembroke. axios.link/4z1KffZ

• RedLattice, a cyber defense-tech company owned by AE Industrial Partners, agreed to a reverse merger with Bold Eagle Acquisition Corp. (Nasdaq: BEAG) at an implied $1.25b valuation (including debt). axios.link/4hu6ofw
 
 
More M&A
 

• BASF (ETR: BAS) said it's in early talks to buy Evonik (ETR: EVK), a rival German specialty chemicals company with around an €8.4b market cap. axios.link/3V4ke0Z

⚡ Geely (HK: 175) agreed to buy a 30% stake in the battery-swapping unit of rival Chinese automaker Nio (HK: 9866), valuing the business at around $2.4b. axios.link/4yn5IjA

• Northern Star Resources (ASX: NST) rejected a US$27.2b takeover offer from South African gold miner Gold Fields (JSE: GFI). axios.link/4rCnH2Q

• Nubank (NYSE: NU) of Brazil is in talks to buy U.K. challenger bank Monzo for between £8b-£10b, per Sky News. axios.link/3VfT875

⚡ Saudi Aramco hired Evercore to restructure its gas unit, which would become a standalone unit that either could go public or secure outside investment at a valuation north of $100b, per Bloomberg. axios.link/4d8Jmty
 
 
Fundraising
 

• Sofinnova Partners raised €82m for its fourth medtech fund. axios.link/4rzYpCg

• Temasek acquired a 9% minority stake in Italian private equity firm FSI. axios.link/4e2HcMi
 
 
It's Personnel
 

• Justine Huang Burns joined Adams Street Partners as a partner focused on venture secondaries. She previously was with Industry Ventures. axios.link/4rAtiGJ

• David Walsh joined HighPost Capital to lead a new aerospace, defense and cybersecurity investment unit. He's a former U.S. Navy intelligence officer who most recently was with FON Advisors. axios.link/3TTZ319
 
 
Final Numbers
 
Data: Financial Modeling Prep; Chart: Dan Primack/Axios

SpaceX this morning successfully launched its Starship rocket into what it hopes will be a 10-hour orbital flight, setting the stage for a massive expansion of its Starlink network and the possible creation of orbital data centers.

By the numbers: SpaceX priced its record-breaking IPO at $135 per share and then saw first trades at $150 per share.

  • Shares are up around 1% as of this writing, just past the $150 mark.
